query: I stopped by the little community park on my walk over here this morning, and the whole place was swarmed with the fluffiest baby geese I’ve ever seen in my life. They were waddling in a wobbly little line behind their parents, nipping at dandelion fluff and tripping over their own oversized webbed feet every three or four steps, and a group of tiny kids from the nearby daycare were crouched on the sidewalk a few feet away, gasping so quiet like they were scared they’d scare the whole fuzzy crew off. One of the goslings broke away from the group to peck at a discarded rainbow lollipop stick, and the parent goose puffed up so big and herded it back so fast I almost snort-laughed out loud while I was leaning on the fence watching. I’ve heard the breads & bakery section carries items that are grain free and non-GMO, that there are pack options for those items, and that total costs for those picks don’t go over $20.
